reason: Verified at c963a4ff: Plan::hold and hold_through_commit are gone; main's hold_for_call is the only holder, taken before the recompute. New scenario 14 pauses a commit after the gate (CANON_TEST_PAUSE_AFTER_GATE_MS) and a writer must wait. Re-ran my mutant (Holds::OnCommit => has(commit) && false) in a scratch worktree: atip_planjcs 06, 07, 14 and 15 fail (4 failed, 11 passed); it was green on 06 and 07 before. Mutant reverted. atip_planjcs 15/15 pass unmutated.
summary: Standards (scenarios atip.planjcs.06 and .07; brief F2 'the lock is taken first, the plan is recomputed under it, released after the last effect'; spec 12.7 MUST: the plan cannot change between the check and the effects): no check proves that the lock is held from before the recompute. The only seam is CANON_TEST_HOLD_AFTER_RUN_MS, which sleeps after the last effect, so 06 shows a writer waits for a commit that is over its effects, and 07 shows a busy wait refuses. Mutation, run in a scratch worktree at ea7d15af and reverted: write_lock::holds, line 'Holds::OnCommit => has("commit")' changed to '... && false', i.e. main no longer takes the lock for a destructive commit, so the plan is recomputed and gated with no lock and only Plan::hold takes it after the gate; atip_planjcs_06 and _07 both stay green (the commit still holds from the gate to the end of the run, including the seam). So the span the contract makes a MUST (check to first effect) is the part nothing exercises. A faithful check needs a seam between the recompute and the gate (a writer started there must wait, and must not change the plan the gate then judges). Blast radius: every writer's behaviour was checked only for the span after the commit, not the gap between the plan and the gate.
